title: A Gravity for the Colony
premise: Yara Oyelaran tends the Genesis Garden aboard the terraforming vessel Meridian, the only living link between two colony fleets that split after a war neither won. When a scout ship returns from deep space with its crew mysteriously aged backward into children, both fleets accuse each other of bioweaponry, and Yara—whose quiet smuggling of letters between worlds made her the only trusted courier—is conscripted to broker peace. She discovers the reversal was caused by a desperate experiment in temporal shielding meant to preserve the fleet's frozen founders, and that the truce expires in ninety days, when the cryo-bays holding half of humanity must be opened by whoever controls the Meridian. In the end, Yara sacrifices her own place in the waking order, choosing to remain behind tending the garden for the born-again crew, while her found family carries her letters—and her love—into the new world.
about_author: Lena Quintana is a former agricultural engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted greenhouse in Lisbon, where she still keeps one wall of growing things at all times.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Establishes her solitary life running supply runs between the rival fleets Vesta and Halcyon, smuggling letters in seed canisters. Introduces the Genesis Garden and her quiet love for Idris, a Vesta comms officer she's never touched. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as purpose.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The scout ship Peregrine docks at Meridian carrying its entire crew de-aged into children with no memories past age eight. Panic spreads through both fleets. Yara recognizes one child as Captain Sefu Adeyemi, who once saved her life. Emotional beat: uncanny dread mixed with tenderness.

chapters.title: Letters in the Bulkheads
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Reveals the letter-smuggling network from his side: he has loved Yara through paper for four years. Vesta command intercepts one of his messages and suspects him of treason. He burns his archive but saves her last letter. Emotional beat: love as contraband.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Commander Vashti Okonkwo's POV. Both fleets' leaders meet aboard neutral Meridian; the cryo-truce that froze the war's losers expires in ninety days, and whoever holds the wake-order decides humanity's future. Vashti, Yara's mentor, is pressured to weaponize the garden. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Investigating the Peregrine's logs, Yara finds traces of temporal shielding experiments run from Meridian itself decades ago—the garden's soil records radiation signatures matching the de-aging event. Someone on her own ship may be responsible. Emotional beat: home becoming suspect.

chapters.title: Nine Fingers
chapters.summary: Child-Sefu's POV. The de-aged captain, trapped in a child's body with an adult's fragmentary instincts, bonds with Yara over the garden. He remembers only one thing clearly: someone named 'the Gardener' told him to go deep and come back changed. Emotional beat: innocence as unreliable witness.

chapters.title: Wake Order
chapters.summary: Vashti's POV. Vesta demands first waking rights; Halcyon threatens to seize the cryo-bays. Vashti secretly drafts a plan to open the bays early under Meridian authority, needing Yara's garden as life support for fifty thousand sleepers. Yara learns she was always meant to be infrastructure. Emotional beat: betrayal by those we serve.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Idris defects across the gap to Meridian, risking execution, to warn Yara that Vesta plans to arrest her as a Halcyon spy. Their first meeting in person is clumsy, real, nothing like their letters. Emotional beat: love arriving late and imperfect.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara and Idris trace the temporal experiments to Dr. Amara Chen, Meridian's founding scientist, whose private lab sits beneath the cryo-bays. Chen is dead—or so the records say—but her AI custodian, VERITY, still runs the shielding array. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: VERITY
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. VERITY reveals Chen's intent: the temporal shield was meant to let founders survive until the colonies healed, but it fired prematurely when the Peregrine strayed into its field. The array could be re-aimed—at the cryo-bays—to buy the truce more time, or weaponized to de-age an entire fleet. Emotional beat: power offered like poison.

chapters.title: The Halcyon Gambit
chapters.summary: Halcyon Admiral Reyes's POV. Reyes learns of the array and moves to seize Meridian, framing Vesta for the Peregrine incident. Her justification chapters reveal how power corrupts even the righteous: she was a war orphan who swore never again, now planning preemption. Emotional beat: idealism curdling into tyranny.

chapters.title: Siege of the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Halcyon marines board Meridian. Yara floods the garden corridors with fog and growth-light to slow them, buying hours, while child-Sefu leads the de-aged crew through maintenance shafts he remembers from his adult life. Emotional beat: the gentle weaponized.

chapters.title: Compromised Frequencies
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Idris broadcasts proof of Chen's original peaceful intent to both fleets, using the old smuggler channels—a network of ordinary people who kept faith across the war. The letter network becomes a resistance network overnight. Emotional beat: small acts compounding.

chapters.title: Vashti's Choice
chapters.summary: Vashti's POV. Offered command of the wake order by whichever side wins, Vashti instead leaks the true truce expiry date publicly, forcing both fleets to negotiate rather than race. She is arrested by Vesta for it. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Minus Forty
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With fifty days left, negotiations stall. VERITY offers Yara the terrible option: fire the shield at the cryo-bays to freeze the truce indefinitely, but the firing will burn out the garden and kill every living thing aboard, including her. Emotional beat: the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: The Child Who Was a Captain
chapters.summary: Child-Sefu's POV. Sefu, aging forward unnaturally fast as the shield destabilizes, recovers enough memory to testify to both fleets about what really happened in deep space. His testimony cracks the mutual accusation—but also confirms the array must fire or fail catastrophically. Emotional beat: truth as last resort.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Vesta and Halcyon delegations meet face-to-face in the garden itself, surrounded by things they jointly grew during the ceasefire talks. A sabotage attempt nearly reignites war; Idris takes a plasma wound shielding Reyes. Emotional beat: enemies sharing oxygen.

chapters.title: What Yara Decided
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara volunteers to stay aboard and hand-fire the shield manually, since automation failed—a death sentence dressed as a shift assignment. She and Idris spend her last night planting a tree that will outlive them both. Emotional beat: love choosing duration over possession.

chapters.title: The Firing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, final entries. Climax: Yara fires the array as both fleets watch, extending the truce a century and stabilizing the de-aged crew's restoration. The garden burns around her—but VERITY, following Chen's deepest protocol, seals Yara in the seed vault's stasis cradle at the moment of ignition. Emotional beat: sacrifice interrupted by grace.

chapters.title: Wake
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The fleets unite to open the cryo-bays together under a shared charter. Idris refuses a seat on the ruling council, asking instead for the gardener's post. The de-aged crew, restored, begin rebuilding. Emotional beat: grief becoming stewardship.

chapters.title: A Gravity for the Colony
chapters.summary: Child-Sefu's POV, years later. Sefu, now grown again and leading the unified colonies, brings his own daughter to Meridian. The garden has regrown wilder than before. In the seed vault, the stasis cradle hums—Yara alive, decades passing outside in minutes. Emotional beat: hope held in suspension.

chapters.title: First Light, Second Spring
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They wake her into a world that kept her letters, planted her trees, and named the charter after the garden. Idris, older now, is waiting with seeds from the first harvest she never saw. She chooses not to lead but to teach—passing the long route to a new generation of couriers. Emotional beat: coming home to a future you built blind.
